newsitem.title: POLAND: Warta issue aimed to set up capital group.
newsitem.headline: Warta issue aimed to set up capital group.

text.p: TUiR Warta SA's new share issue is aimed at setting up a capital group encompassing the insurance company and some banks, Warta's spokesman Jacek Likowski said.
Likowski told Reuters that through the new issue of 865,380 to 2,596,139 registered shares Warta intended to take part in the privatisation of a Polish bank, but it did not disclose its name.
"The direct aim of the issue is ... active participation in the privatisation of one of the bigger Polish banks and creating a capital banking-insurance group," Likowski said.

The Warta issue is directed to two minority shareholders as well as Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy SA (BPH), Kredyt Bank SA, and state-owned Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), slated for privatisation in April 1997.
Likowski did not say how the shares would be divided between the five institutions.
Earlier this year PBK, Kredyt Bank and listed Polish Development Bank (PBR) began creating equity links.
PBK has acquired a 25 percent stake in Kredyt Bank and is about to finalise an acquisition of almost 33 percent of PBR.
In turn PBR and Kredyt have said they wanted to buy significant stakes in PBK during its privatisation.
Likowski said Warta was considering another share issue next year for a foreign investor -- an insurance company -- but declined to give any details.

Currently Warta has 3.46 million shares and its main stockholders are the state treasury, with a 34.7 percent stake, Elektrim with 10.1 percent, Anna Wozniak with 5.8 percent and Kulczyk Holding with 5.2 percent.
